searches.association: Single query; results are observed tool output, not measured Google positions.

sources.findings: Google separates calendar ownership transfer, event ownership change, moving an event, and copying. Primary calendars cannot transfer; current owner can transfer a secondary calendar. Work/school calendar ownership stays within the organization. Recipient must accept emailed transfer within 60 days; sender remains owner until acceptance. Account deletion deletes owned calendars. More than 200 guests prevents event transfer; Meet policies may change.
sources.boundary: Google computer instructions, not Cloud controls or cross-provider ownership migration. Do not generalize secondary calendar eligibility without the current-owner restriction.

sources.findings: Computer imports ICS/CSV into a chosen calendar, default primary. ZIP requires extracting individual ICS. Imports omit guests/conference data, are not ongoing sync; CSV repeats may become individual events.
sources.boundary: Already covered in export guide. Source line35 unexpectedly says vCard for Apple, inconsistent with its ICS/CSV import section and Apple's ICS export instructions; do not repeat that line as calendar-format advice.

sources.findings: Personal and work/school web flows distinguish Upload from file, selected destination, and Subscribe from web. Import is a snapshot; subscription updates may take more than 24 hours.
sources.boundary: Web instructions, not native iPhone Outlook or Cloud UI. Refresh suggestions are not deadlines. Already covered conceptually.

sources.findings: Mac exports individual calendars as ICS, imports into selected calendar, and supports archive ICBU whose import replaces current calendar data. Provider-backed calendars stored on provider servers do not require manual device-to-device transfer.
sources.boundary: Mac instructions, not an iPhone export menu. Existing guide already has these distinctions.

discovery_scope: Four queries, 31 explicit result URLs. Four official provider documentation bodies reviewed. Other observed URLs remain discovery/snippet-only. No independent app competitor body newly reviewed in this bounded batch; Apple/Google/Microsoft are provider primary sources. No failed original corpus URL retried.

recommendation.task: Before retiring a Google account, decide whether you need a copied schedule or an ownership handoff, and verify acceptance before treating the handoff as finished.
recommendation.rationale: Current export guide covers import formats, destinations, representative checks and missing meeting metadata, but not ownership-transfer eligibility or acceptance. A short Google-specific decision paragraph/FAQ adds a distinct actionable decision without creating another migration page.
suggested_scope: Add a brief subsection near safe import explaining that export/import copies event data; it is not an ownership transfer.
For a Google secondary-calendar handoff, point to current official computer instructions and require current owner/same-organization rule for work/school accounts; primary calendars cannot transfer.
Check that the recipient accepted ownership; sending the email alone is not completion. Google permits 60 days and retains old ownership until acceptance.
Keep Google-specific ownership restrictions separate from iCloud/Outlook migration. Do not imply a cross-provider transfer preserves guests, conferencing or organizational rights.
recommendation.not_recommended: No standalone iCloud-to-Google, Google-to-Outlook, or iPhone-migration synonym page; current export guide already addresses the shared file/import task.
